title: Now Hiring: Sidekick
text:
Now hiring! Captain Kindness is looking for a {adjective} sidekick to help around town. You will work with Captain Kindness every Saturday from nine until lunchtime.

Your jobs will include helping kittens down from trees, carrying groceries for neighbors, and finding lost {plural noun}. You must be able to run {adverb}, hop over a {noun}, and {verb} without getting dizzy.

Every sidekick gets a cape, a mask, and a bright {color} belt with {number} pockets. Captain Kindness will also teach you the secret hero handshake. It uses your {body part} and a little bit of {verb ending in ing}.

Our last sidekick {past tense verb} so much that he needed a long vacation. To apply, please bring a smile and a {adjective} sandwich to the library on Tuesday.

title: My First Week with Super Powers
text:
Dear Diary,
On Monday I woke up and found out I have super powers! I can fly, but only about as high as a {noun}. I can also see through walls, but only if I wiggle my {body part} first.

On Tuesday I used my powers for good. I helped Mrs. Kim find her {adjective} glasses. They were on top of her head. Then I flew to the park and {past tense verb} with the ducks.

On Wednesday I tried to {verb} faster than a train. I went so fast that my socks flew off and landed in a pile of {plural noun}. Mom says superheroes still have to pick up their socks.

Today I made my own cape out of a blanket and {number} {plural noun}. Tomorrow I will practice {verb ending in ing} and flying {adverb} at the same time.

title: Rules at Superhero Headquarters
text:
Welcome to Superhero Headquarters! Please read these rules before you put on your cape.

Rule one: No flying in the hallways. Last week Thunder Girl flew into a {noun} and tipped over the lemonade. Rule two: Please hang your cape on a hook, not on the {plural noun}. Rule three: Please do not {verb} on the new carpet in muddy boots.

Rule four: The kitchen is for snacks only. Our cook, Mr. Fox, makes a {adjective} sandwich with cheese and {plural noun}. Please eat it {adverb}, and do not use your heat vision to warm it up.

Rule five: When the hero phone rings, answer it right away. Someone may need help finding a lost {animal} or carrying {number} heavy bags. Every hero must be ready to go, even while {verb ending in ing}. Thank you, and have a {adjective} day of helping!

title: Local Hero Rescues Kitten Again
text:
Good morning, this is Radio Ten with today's news. For the third time this week, the hero known as Zoom Girl has rescued a kitten named Muffin from the big oak tree on Pine Street.

Neighbors say Muffin climbs the tree every morning to look at the {plural noun}. Then she gets nervous and meows {adverb} until help arrives. Today, Zoom Girl flew up, lifted Muffin out of a {adjective} nest, and {past tense verb} back down to the sidewalk.

"Muffin is a good kitten," Zoom Girl told our reporter. "She just likes to {verb} in high places." Muffin's owner, Mr. Lee, thanked Zoom Girl with a hug and {number} plates of {food}.

Next week, the town will put a {noun} at the bottom of the tree. Zoom Girl says she will keep {verb ending in ing} until Muffin learns to climb down by herself. That is all for now. Stay {adjective}, everyone!

title: Breakfast of Heroes
text:
Every superhero needs a good breakfast before a long day of helping. This is the famous Hero Smoothie that Captain Comet drinks every morning.

First, put two bananas and a cup of milk into the blender. Next, add a big handful of {plural noun} and one {adjective} {noun}. Captain Comet says this part gives you your super strength.

Now flip the switch and blend it {adverb} for {number} seconds. If the blender begins to {verb}, that is normal. Pour the smoothie into your tallest cup and top it with a sprinkle of {plural noun}.

Drink it all in one sip while {verb ending in ing} on one foot. Captain Comet says it tastes a lot like {food}. Then wash your cup, put on your cape, and go have a {adjective} day!

title: Meet Captain Helpful
text:
This month, our class got to interview Captain Helpful, the friendliest hero in town. He came to our classroom in a {color} cape and sat in Ms. Gray's chair.

First, we asked how he got his powers. "I ate a {adjective} sandwich at the library," he said. "The next morning, I could lift {number} {plural noun} with one finger." Then we asked about his favorite power. "Flying," he said. "But I also like to {verb} really fast."

Next, we asked about his best rescue ever. He said a little boy once lost his {noun} at the park. Captain Helpful searched {adverb} for three hours and finally found it under a slide.

Last, we asked what kids can do to be heroes. "Be kind, share your {plural noun}, and help your family," he said. "And never stop {verb ending in ing}." Then he waved and {past tense verb} out the door.

title: Letter Home from Hero Camp
text:
Dear Grandma,
Hero camp is the best place ever! My cabin is called Blue Lightning, and it has {number} bunk beds. My camp leader is named Captain Sunny. She is very {adjective} and can fly backwards.

Every morning we practice our powers. Yesterday I practiced super strength by lifting a {noun} over my head. My friend Leo practiced being invisible, but we could still see his {body part}. In the afternoon we learned how to {verb} on the soft grass.

At dinner we eat hero stew, which is mostly carrots and {plural noun}. After that we sit by the campfire and sing songs about {plural noun}. Captain Sunny sings {adverb}. Last night I {past tense verb} so hard that I fell asleep before the song ended.

I will be home on Sunday. Please save me a slice of pie and tell the dog I have been {verb ending in ing} every day.
Love,
Ava

title: How to Design Your Own Cape
text:
Every hero needs a good cape. Here is how to make your very own.

First, find an old towel or blanket. Ask a grown-up first! Lay it flat on the floor and decorate it with markers, stickers, and {plural noun}. Many heroes like to draw a big {noun} in the middle. That is called your hero symbol.

Next, choose your hero colors. Most heroes pick red or blue, but you can pick {color} if you want. Then give yourself a hero name, like Captain {silly word} or The {adjective} Wonder. Ask your grown-up to clip the cape to the back of your shirt with a clothespin.

Now practice your hero moves. Stand tall, put your hands on your hips, and get ready to {verb}. A real hero always walks {adverb} and helps anyone who is {verb ending in ing}. When you are done, hang your cape next to your {plural noun} so it is ready for tomorrow.

title: Superhero Talent Show Tonight
text:
Attention, everyone! The yearly Superhero Talent Show starts tonight at six o'clock in the town park. Bring a blanket, a snack, and your whole family.

Twelve heroes will show off their amazing powers. Rocket Ron will fly in circles while holding a {noun}. Ice Lady will make a snowman shaped like a {animal}. Mighty Max will lift {number} {plural noun} at the same time, and then he will {verb} for the crowd.

The judges are Mayor Bell, a librarian, and a very {adjective} dog named Scout. Scout will bark {adverb} when he likes an act. The winner gets a golden cape and a whole year of free {plural noun}.

There will also be a snack table with popcorn, apples, and {food}. Please clap loudly, cheer kindly, and do not try {verb ending in ing} on the stage. Last year a hero did that, and the stage {past tense verb} for an hour.

title: Postcard from a Hero on Vacation
text:
Dear Sidekick,
Greetings from Sunny Beach! Even heroes need a vacation. I am staying in a little hotel shaped like a {noun}, and every morning I eat pancakes with {plural noun} on top.

I am trying very hard to relax, but it is not easy. Yesterday a beach ball floated away, so I {past tense verb} into the waves and brought it back. Then a little boy dropped his ice cream, so I flew {adverb} to the shop and got him a new one. Today I helped a {adjective} crab find its way home.

Tomorrow I plan to {verb} in the sand all day and not rescue anything at all. Please water my plants and feed my {animal} while I am gone. Do not let it eat any {plural noun}.
See you soon,
Captain Starlight
P.S. I got sand in my {body part}.
